title: Air Masses, Fronts and Weather
seo_title: Grade 6 Air Masses Worksheets: Fronts, Air Pressure and Weather Changes
standard_text: Collect data to provide evidence for how the motions and complex interactions of air masses results in changes in weather conditions.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on air masses and weather (NGSS MS-ESS2-5): maritime and continental air masses, cold and warm fronts, high and low pressure, and weather data tables. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Weather changes when air masses meet.
key_sub: Cold fronts bring storms and then cooler air. Warm fronts bring light rain and then warmer air. Low pressure means clouds.
body_html:
How to think about it

An air mass is a huge body of air with about the same temperature and humidity. It takes on the conditions of where it forms: maritime (over ocean, humid) or continental (over land, dry); tropical (warm) or polar (cold).

Air masses move and meet at fronts, where weather changes:

  • Cold front: A cold air mass pushes under a warm air mass and forces it up quickly. Weather: thunderstorms or heavy rain, then cooler and drier weather.
  • Warm front: A warm air mass slides up over a cold air mass. Weather: light, steady rain or drizzle, then warmer and more humid weather.
  • Stationary front: Two air masses meet but neither moves much. Weather: many days of cloudy, wet weather.
  • Occluded front: A cold front catches up to a warm front and lifts the warm air off the ground. Weather: clouds and precipitation, often cooler.

High pressure usually means clear, calm weather. Low pressure usually means clouds and precipitation.

Example

The temperature drops 10 °C after a thunderstorm. What passed?

Sharp drop + storm.

Answer: a cold front

Example

An air mass forms over the Gulf of Mexico. What is it like?

Ocean = humid.

Near the tropics = warm.

Answer: warm and humid

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a cold front brings warmer weather.
  • Thinking low pressure means clear skies.
  • Forgetting that air masses keep the conditions of where they formed.

faq.q: What weather does a cold front bring?
faq.a: Often thunderstorms or heavy rain, followed by cooler, drier weather.

faq.q: What do high and low pressure mean for weather?
faq.a: High pressure usually brings clear, calm weather. Low pressure usually brings clouds and precipitation.

items.q: Which air mass would bring warm, humid weather to the southeastern United States?

maritime tropical air from the Gulf of Mexico
items.e: Maritime = ocean (humid), tropical = warm.

items.q: What is a front?
c: the boundary where two different air masses meet
items.e: Weather often changes at fronts.

items.q: Ethan reads: “Two air masses meet but neither moves much.” What kind of front is this?
items.e: That describes a stationary front.

items.q: After a cold front passes, the weather usually becomes

items.q: Why do cold fronts often bring thunderstorms?

items.e: Fast-rising air builds storm clouds.
